To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcript accumulations of pea Gα1 and α2 subunits of heterotrimetric G-protein, the activities of peroxidases, and H2O2 and ABA accumulation were stimulated by OKC and T44 individually and co-inoculated with pea plants, and the stimulation was positively correlated with stomatal closure and reduced conidial development of E. pisi on pea leaves.

the transcript accumulation patterns, peroxidase activities and phenol contents were positively correlated with each other in pea leaves under the stimulus of P. fluorescens and T. asperellum and the correlation was further correlated with stomatal closure at early stage and reduced E. pisin conidial development in the leaves.

Pseudomonas fluorescence (OKC) and Trichodermae asperellum (T42) enhance the expression of Gα1 and2 subunits of pea heterotrimeric g-protein during E. pisi infection and this is possibly mediated through jasmonate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of heterotrimer G proteins in pea during E. pisi infection in the presence of the rhizosphere microbes OKC and T 42.
the role of heterotrimer G-protein and its subunits in the interaction of two soil-inhibiting microbes and a biotrophic pathogenic fungus with pea.
the role of heterotrimer G-protein in pea in the interaction with two soil microbes and a biotroph pathogen and we suggest the involvement of G-protein in the signal transduction in this interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heterotrimer G protein is a part of the plant defense system in pea against E. pisi and the microbes OKC and T 42 are able to stimulate the Gα1/2 subunits of G-protein and the JA-mediated pathway to induce the defense system in pea leaves.

the microbes (P. fluorescens and T. asperellum) stimulate transcript accumulations and activities of the pea heterotrimeric protein, peroxidase activities and accumulation of phenols in pea under the biotroph (E. pisi) challenge, which finally led to reduced development of E. pisi on pea leaves.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rhizosphere microbes (OKC & T42) enhance the expression of the G-protein subunits in pea leaves, which may lead to enhanced peroxidase activities and phenolic production in pea leaves, and finally to reduced Erysiphe development.
Gα subunits of the pea heterotrimeric protein are activated in response to the rhizosphere microbes, particularly under the stimulation of T42.
heterotrimeric proteins are involved in the microbe-induced resistance to biotrophs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gα subunits of the pea heterotrimeric protein may be involved in the microbe-mediated suppression of E. pisi on pea.
heterotrimeric proteins are involved in plant responses to microbes and the Gα subunits are the key players in this interaction.
the Gα subunit of heterotrimer G protein may be a potential target to engineer for disease resistance in crop plants.
